"Queens separated by more than one row MAY share a long diagonal; this is not the ordinary chess N-queens diagonal rule." This is a crucial distinction. It means if I have a queen at (r, c) and another at (r+2, c), that's fine. But (r, c) and (r+1, c+1) is forbidden. So, for any two queens in rows $i$ and $j$ where $|i-j|=1$, we must have $|col_i - col_j| > 1$. This effectively means no two queens can be on a diagonal if they are in adjacent rows.
